synthesis.summary: The panel converges strongly: the PR fixes a real metadata/$ref propagation bug across clone chains, but the implementation ships with unstated invariants, JSON.stringify used as a structural-equality primitive in a hot loop, a silent doubling of override invocations (test expectation flipped from 6 to 12 under a test still named "do not run on references"), and debug scratch (play.ts) committed to the tree. The new Seen.ref / Seen.parent fields overlap with no documented contract, and flattenRef now performs three to four distinct mutations on a shared schema object with order-dependent effects and a recursion guard (seen.ref = null) that only covers one of two edges. Required before merge: state flattenRef's pre/post/termination invariant, replace stringify-equality with a defined structural compare or track key provenance at assignment time, document or revert the override-on-parent contract change, drop or relocate play.ts, and justify the mini/classic { parent: true } realignment with a substitutability test. The fileProcessor refactor (hoisting shared props above anyOf) is a genuine simplification but deserves a one-line spec comment and ideally its own patch.

issues.description: JSON.stringify used as structural-equality primitive for de-duplication inside finalize hot loop
issues.detail: Two new blocks decide whether to delete a child key with JSON.stringify(schema[key]) === JSON.stringify(refSeen.def![key]). This is order-sensitive on object keys, lossy on undefined/NaN/Infinity/BigInt, throws on cycles, allocates two strings per comparison, and runs O(subtree-size) inside a per-seen-schema loop on the JSON-schema generation hot path. Replace with a defined structural-equality helper, or — better — track at assignment time which keys came from inheritance vs the child so the dedupe becomes set-difference instead of stringify-compare.

issues.description: Override-count test expectation doubled from 6 to 12 with no justification; silent contract change
issues.detail: The previous code guarded ctx.override(...) with if (!seen.isParent); the new code removes that guard and the test 'override: do not run on references' was updated from toBe(6) to toBe(12). User-supplied override callbacks will now fire on parent schemas in the clone chain, which is an observable breaking change to a public contract. The test title still asserts the old behavior. Either restore leaf-only invocation, or document the new contract in the override JSDoc/changelog and rename the test.

issues.description: Seen.ref and Seen.parent overlap with no stated contract; flattenRef recursion lacks invariant and termination proof
issues.detail: Seen now carries two near-identical pointers (ref, parent) whose legal combinations are encoded only in conditional logic spread across process() and finalize(). flattenRef recurses on both seen.ref and seen.parent; the seen.ref = null sentinel blocks re-entry on the ref edge but parent is never nulled, so termination depends on graph shape rather than a decreasing measure. Write the Seen contract (legal states of ref/parent, what null vs undefined mean), state flattenRef's precondition/postcondition/invariant, and either add an explicit visited-set parameter or prove the existing sentinel covers both edges. Consider a single discriminated inheritance descriptor instead of two overlapping fields.

issues.description: flattenRef complects four concerns into one mutating function
issues.detail: flattenRef now (1) inherits ref properties, (2) restores child overrides, (3) strips parent-only keys on the refinement branch via set-difference against _cached, (4) dedupes against extracted $def via stringify equality, and (5) propagates $ref from parent in a second recursive pass. These run as a sequence of mutations on the shared schema object with order-dependent effects and no stated invariants between phases. Refactor so the final schema is computed as a pure function of named inputs (own props, inherited props, relationship-kind, extracted-ref-target) and assigned once; or at minimum extract the two near-identical dedupe loops (line ~418 and ~444, which both skip $ref/allOf and both use stringify) into a single helper.

issues.description: process() reorders parent handling without documenting the new invariant
issues.detail: Previously when a parent existed, the parent was processed first and the child's own processor was skipped; now the child's processor always runs first and the parent is recorded separately. This is a real data-flow contract change: processors that previously could assume the parent's seen entry was populated when they ran no longer can, and any processor previously bypassed for child schemas now executes. The reversed iteration in the final loop interacts with this ordering. Document the new invariant above process() — what each pass sees, which processor 'wins' on key collisions, and the consequence for idempotence.

issues.description: play.ts committed as a debug scratchpad with a relative source import
issues.detail: play.ts switched from `import * as z from 'zod/v4'` to `./packages/zod/src/index.js` and is now hand-rolled console.log debugging of the bug under repair. It is the author's working scratchpad, couples a top-level file to the monorepo internal layout, and is evidence the change was validated by eyeballing stdout. Revert play.ts or move it under a tests/repros/ folder with real assertions; it should not be part of the merged diff.

issues.description: mini/schemas.ts silently enables { parent: true } previously commented out, with no substitutability test
issues.detail: The mini variant uncomments { parent: true } so mini.check now establishes a parent link matching classic. The original comment was presumably there for a reason; the reason has been deleted along with the comment. This is a postcondition change for any mini consumer that depended on the old behavior (iterating _zod.parent chains, isParent not being set, etc.). Either document why it is now safe and add a mini-vs-classic equivalence test (e.g. on the new wrapper-with-id case), or revert.

issues.description: Refinement detection via (zodSchema as any)._zod.parent === ref duplicates the source of truth already on seen
issues.detail: process() already records result.parent = parent and copies it onto seen.parent. finalize then reaches back through _zod.parent with an `as any` cast to recompute the same fact ('this edge is the parent edge'), inviting the two sources to diverge under cloning. Read from seen.parent === ref instead and drop the cast, or document why the two cannot diverge. Ideally promote the relationship to a named, set-once value on seen (e.g. seen.relationship: 'refinement' | 'wrapper' | 'inherited') so finalize becomes a pure dispatch.

issues.description: isParentRef branch deletes keys via set-difference against a pre-merge snapshot with the invariant unstated
issues.detail: After Object.assign(schema, refSchema); Object.assign(schema, _cached); the isParentRef branch walks every key in schema and deletes anything not in _cached, on the assumption 'child is a refinement and inherits nothing structural from its parent.' Any property added to the child implicitly by an earlier processor pass would be stripped. The intended invariant ('after this block, schema contains only the child's own keys plus $ref/allOf') is plausible but never written down, and the asymmetry with the non-parent branch (where parent properties are kept) is unjustified. Write the invariant in a comment or, better, fix the model so intent isn't reconstructed via set-difference.

issues.description: PR bundles three independent changes; should be split
issues.detail: This is three patches in one: (1) the parent-tracking fix in to-json-schema.ts + classic/schemas.ts + the wrapper-id test, (2) the fileProcessor hoist-shared-props refactor and its snapshot update, (3) the mini/schemas.ts { parent: true } enablement. They have independent justifications, independent risk, and independent bisect value. Split them so each can land or be reverted on its own merit.

issues.description: fileProcessor refactor is correct but anyOf branches now lack standalone validation properties; document the merge semantics
issues.detail: Hoisting shared props (type, format, contentEncoding, minLength, maxLength) to the root and reducing each anyOf branch to just { contentMediaType: m } is a real simplification, but weakens each branch's standalone postcondition — consumers that read schema.anyOf[0] in isolation no longer see the string constraints. Per JSON Schema this is fine (anyOf composes with sibling keywords), but the diff drops the typed JSONSchema.StringSchema return on the map callback and the codebase explicitly targets draft 07/04 and OpenAPI 3.0 elsewhere in flattenRef. Add a one-line comment naming the invariant ('shared file constraints at root; per-mime contentMediaType in anyOf; relies on sibling-merge semantics') so a future contributor doesn't 'helpfully' put the shared props back into each branch.

issues.description: Seen.ref type narrowed inconsistently with Seen.parent; absent vs sentinel vs set is unclear
issues.detail: Seen.ref tightened from `$ZodType | undefined | null` to `$ZodType | null`, while Seen.parent uses `$ZodType | undefined`. ref now encodes three states (absent, null-sentinel for 'already processed', and pointing-to-a-schema) but the type doesn't distinguish them, and the two adjacent fields use opposite conventions for 'absent.' Pick one convention and document it, or model the state with a small discriminated union / named-state enum.
